name: Complex transition kit: one envelope-mode LFO (≈2 bars) drives global pitch and also the rate of a second LFO (nested acceleration) for distortion drive or volume stutters; layer a sine downer, a high stutter riser, a multi-osc main riser (levels/drive/filter/reverb wet all under LFO1), a detuned atmosphere bed, then group with automated high-passes so early bars favour the downer/stutter and later bars favour the main rise
goal: Build a cinematic riser/downer stack that feels more complex than a single pitch sweep: use one master envelope-LFO as a timeline that both bends pitch and accelerates a second LFO (nested rate modulation) for stutter or grit, then layer contrasting roles (downer, high stutter, main rise, atmosphere) and automate high-passes between subgroups. Delta vs risers-impacts cluster: LFO1→LFO2-frequency nesting as the acceleration engine, plus the explicit multi-role layer kit and HPF automation between layers rather than a single whoosh or Shepard stack.

source.title: How To Sound Design Complex Risers (using Vital)

prerequisites: Synth with ≥2 oscillators, unison/smear, global pitch/transpose, ≥2 LFOs (envelope mode + free-running rate in seconds), mod matrix, distortion, filter, EQ, compressor, reverb

outputs.name: transition_fx
outputs.description: Layered riser/downer/atmosphere transition ready to place before a hit

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Map movement to filter, level, drive and spectral morph — keep intentional musical pitch bends on a dedicated global-pitch lane, not random vibrato.
Low-cut competing layers when a downer owns the sub.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.
Steady pitch: leave out intentional pitch-drift LFOs unless the brief asks for tape wobble (Matt prefers steady pitch).

steps.action: Downer layer: sine on osc 1. Put LFO1 in envelope mode for ~2 bars into global pitch/transpose so the tone falls. Enable distortion; put LFO2 on drive amount, set LFO2 rate in seconds, and route LFO1 → LFO2 rate so grit accelerates as the pitch falls.

On the downer add a second oscillator with a few unison voices and smear; route LFO1 to its spectral-morph (or wavetable position). Low-pass / EQ so the full bright spectrum arrives only near the end of the 2 bars; give the amp a little attack.
steps.expect: Downer blooms spectrally as it falls

steps.action: High stutter riser (new patch): sine pitched up several octaves, light unison, LFO1 envelope → global pitch upward. LFO2 → oscillator level for stutter; again LFO1 → LFO2 rate (seconds) so the stutter speeds up. Filter highs early; optionally bring osc 2 in under the same LFO2 level for bite.

Main riser: LFO1 envelope (~2 bars) to global pitch and to the level of all oscillators (bias one osc louder). Spread osc pitches (e.g. +2 oct / dominant mid / −1 oct). LFO1 also to distortion drive, to a high-shelf or filter cutoff, and to reverb mix starting near 100% wet then decreasing while size grows.

Duplicate the main riser and pitch the copy higher (or down an octave for a variant); trim noise. Add an atmosphere patch: heavily detuned oscillators, lots of reverb, mild LFO1→global pitch rise, optional noise and higher-octave detuned layers.

Group the stack. Automate high-passes so early bars favour the downer + high stutter (other layers darker), then open them; high-pass the downer later so it does not dominate the end. Bus EQ (cut mud), light compression and a limiter; balance levels.

verification: LFO2 rate audibly accelerates when LFO1 rises (nested).
Downer, stutter riser, main riser and atmosphere are separately audible roles.
Early bars are darker / HPF-managed; end is full-spectrum without sub mud from every layer.
